title: Infinitesimal quotients on arbitrary affine charts of a formal completion
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $X_n$ be the closed subscheme defined by $\mathcal I^n$, with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I^n$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ put $I=\mathcal I(V)$ and $C=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The ringed spaces $\operatorname{Spf}C$ glue to a locally Noetherian adic formal scheme $\mathfrak X$ with underlying space $|X_1|$. Here $\operatorname{Spf}C$ has the primes containing $IC$, with the subspace topology from $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and sheaf $\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}(C/(IC)^n)}$. The kernel of the map $\mathcal O_{\mathfrak X}\to\mathcal O_{X_1}$ is a coherent ideal of definition $\mathfrak J$; on these charts it is associated to $IC$. For every formal affine open $U=\operatorname{Spf}R\subseteq\mathfrak X$, where $R$ is Noetherian, complete and separated for a finitely generated ideal $K$, there is a finitely generated ideal $J\subseteq R$ whose associated completed ideal sheaf is $\mathfrak J|_U$; the powers of $J$ define the same topology as those of $K$, the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/J^n$ is an isomorphism, and $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J^n)$ is canonically the restriction of $X_n$ to the open subset $|U|\subseteq|X_n|$ for every $n\geq1$. These identifications respect the quotient transition maps. No quasi-excellence hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0AHY (section-formal-schemes-EGA, formal spectra and sheaves), 0GXU (definition-completion-subspace), 0GXX (lemma-affine-formal-completion-subspace-types), 0GXY (lemma-formal-completion-subspace-types). Coherent ideal and arbitrary formal affine quotient dictionary: EGA I, §10.8, §10.10 (archival copy WANTED); EGA III.1 §5.1.1 explicitly recalls coherence of completed coherent modules. This supporting statement includes the affine ideal correspondence needed to pass beyond the chosen completion cover.

proof.text: Fix an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its ring is Noetherian, and $I=\mathcal I(V)$ is finite. The affine product-and-quotient dictionary gives $\mathcal I^n(V)=I^n$ and $X_n|_V=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$. The completion $C$ is Noetherian, complete and separated for $IC$, and its projection gives $C/(IC)^n\cong A/I^n$ for every positive $n$. All these isomorphisms are induced by the projections, so commute with quotient transitions. Apply the completion theorem to the module $A$; its module isomorphisms are ring isomorphisms because the projections preserve multiplication.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA; explicit assembly of completion charts and coherent ideals

proof.text: On $Z=|X_1|$ form the ring sheaf $\mathcal O=\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_{X_n}$, with componentwise operations. Limits are sectionwise (the index category is the small category of positive integers). Restriction to $Z\cap V$ gives the inverse limit of the structure sheaves of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$, hence, by Step 1, precisely $\operatorname{Spf}C$. This constructs all charts inside one ringed space; their identifications on overlaps are restrictions of the same sheaf, so satisfy the cocycle identity even when $V\cap V\prime$ is not affine. The charts from a finite affine cover of $X$ cover $Z$, proving the locally Noetherian adic formal-scheme assertion.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA; explicit assembly of completion charts and coherent ideals

proof.text: Let $\pi_n:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_{X_n}$ be the projections. On a completion chart $\operatorname{Spf}C$, apply the formal affine module equivalence to $0\to(IC)^n\to C\to C/(IC)^n\to0$. Since this quotient is killed by $(IC)^n$, its completed associated sheaf is its ordinary associated sheaf on $V(IC)$: its quotient system is constant for indices at least $n$. Thus $\pi_n$ is surjective and its kernel is $((IC)^n)^\triangle$. In particular $\mathfrak J=\ker\pi_1$ is locally $(IC)^\triangle$ and coherent. Tensor compatibility and exactness identify its $n$th image power with $((IC)^n)^\triangle$. Therefore globally $\ker\pi_n=\mathfrak J^n$ and $\mathcal O/\mathfrak J^n=\mathcal O_{X_n}$. On these charts $IC$ is an ideal of definition; this is a local property, so $\mathfrak J$ is an ideal of definition.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA; explicit assembly of completion charts and coherent ideals

proof.text: Now take any formal affine $U=\operatorname{Spf}(R,K)$. Restrict $\mathfrak J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O$ to $U$ and apply the exact equivalence and its specified global-sections quasi-inverse. It gives an injection of a finite module into $R$, hence a finitely generated ideal $J=\Gamma(U,\mathfrak J)\subseteq R$, and an identification $J^\triangle=\mathfrak J|_U$ respecting the inclusion. Images of multiplication maps correspond under the tensor-compatible exact equivalence, so $(J^n)^\triangle=(\mathfrak J|_U)^n$. In particular $(R/J^n)^\triangle=(\mathcal O/\mathfrak J^n)|_U$, with their actual quotient maps.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA; explicit assembly of completion charts and coherent ideals

proof.text: Let $x\in U$ have prime $\mathfrak p_x\supseteq K$ of $R$ and stalk $\mathcal O_x$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$. (i) If $f\in R$, $f\notin\mathfrak p_x$, the principal-refinement theorem makes restriction to $D(f)\cap U$ the map $R\to R_f\to R_{\{f\}}$, so $f$ is invertible there and $f_x\notin\mathfrak m_x$. (ii) If $k\in K$, then $k_x\in\mathfrak m_x$: it maps to $0$ in the nonzero stalk $(R/K)_{\mathfrak p_x}$ of the first projection $\mathcal O|_U\to\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)}$. By Step 3, $\mathfrak J_x$ is the kernel of the surjection $\mathcal O_x\to\mathcal O_{X_1,x}$ onto a nonzero local ring; so $\mathfrak J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x$, and $\mathfrak m_x$ maps into the maximal ideal. By (i), each $j\in J=\mathfrak J(U)$ lies in every prime containing $K$, so $J\subseteq\sqrt K$ by the radical lemma. Conversely, $U$ is covered by its intersections with the completion charts $\operatorname{Spf}C$, and principal opens $D(t)\cap\operatorname{Spf}C$ form a basis there; as $|U|\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)$ is quasi-compact, choose finitely many $W_i=D(t_i)\cap\operatorname{Spf}C_i\subseteq U$ covering $U$. By Step 1, $X_1$ over $V_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C_i/IC_i)$, so $\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{X_1})=B_i=(C_i/IC_i)_{t_i}$, whose primes are the points of $W_i$. For $k\in K$, (ii) puts the image of $k$ in $B_i$ in every prime, so it is nilpotent (radical lemma for the zero ideal): $k^{N_i}|_{W_i}\in\ker(\mathcal O(W_i)\to\mathcal O_{X_1}(W_i))=\mathfrak J(W_i)$. For $N=\max N_i$ the sheaf property of $\mathfrak J\subseteq\mathcal O$ gives $k^N\in J$, so $K\subseteq\sqrt J$. As $K$ and $J$ are finitely generated, the power lemma gives $a,b\geq1$ with $K^a\subseteq J$ and $J^b\subseteq K$; taking powers gives cofinality of the two filtrations on $R$. Only the ringed-space chart isomorphism of $U$ is used, no topology on $\mathcal O$.

proof.text: Cofinality proves $J$-adic completeness directly. For a compatible family $x_n\in R/J^n$, choose representatives $r_n\in R$. For $m\geq n$, $r_m-r_n\in J^n$. Since $J^{bt}\subseteq K^t$, these representatives are $K$-Cauchy and have a unique limit $r\in R$. To check $r\bmod J^n=x_n$, choose $t$ with $K^t\subseteq J^n$ (use $K^{an}\subseteq J^n$); a sufficiently late $r_m$ agrees with $r$ modulo $K^t$ and with $r_n$ modulo $J^n$. Thus $r-r_n\in J^n$. If $r$ maps to zero, then $r\in\bigcap J^n\subseteq\bigcap K^t=0$. This proves that the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim R/J^n$ is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AHY, section-formal-schemes-EGA; explicit assembly of completion charts and coherent ideals

proof.text: Because $K^{an}\subseteq J^n$, the $K$-adic quotient system of $R/J^n$ is eventually constant. Therefore $(R/J^n)^\triangle$ is the ordinary structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J^n)$ on the common space $V(J)=V(K)$. Step 4 and $\mathcal O/\mathfrak J^n=\mathcal O_{X_n}$ identify this ringed space with the restriction of $X_n$ to $|U|$. These are isomorphisms of schemes because they identify the ordinary locally ringed spaces. For $m\geq n$, both maps to level $n$ are induced by $\pi_n$ and $R\twoheadrightarrow R/J^n$: they send a local residue of $r$ at level $m$ to the residue of the same $r$ at level $n$. These residues generate on principal opens, so the maps agree as sheaf maps. No quasi-excellence assumption entered any step.
